correctness.rationale: For a pairing of reversed arcs, every cyclic triple has a reversed outer edge and the full face set is determined by the corresponding forbidden triples. An outside vertex yields a cone; separated arcs form a join of two single-arc complexes, nested arcs a suspension plus one edge, and crossing arcs either collapse by domination or reduce to the explicit 5-vertex collapsible core or 4-vertex circle. Each argument is integral for all n>=4. Direct enumeration for n=4..9 verifies 756 configurations and the ten elementary crossing collapses, without substituting finite data for proof.

value.rationale: Reversing the same number of vertex-disjoint arcs in an otherwise transitive tournament can cause a contractible, one-circle, three-sphere or mixed circle-plus-two-sphere result. Necessary and sufficient endpoint-order/gap conditions give a complete natural phase diagram, rather than an arbitrary slice of small-order computations. This reveals genuinely structural sensitivity of directed-flag homotopy to sparse orientation changes.
